cases.name: Hiawayi D-Iland Robinson
cases.about:
Her Find-a-Grave said, "Hiawayi D-Iland Robinson native, resident of Mobile, Alabama and a 3rd grader at Collins-Rhodes Elementary School, was born September 24, 2005 to her mother Yosha Populus and her father Hiawatha Robinson, Jr. On an assignment from God, Hiawayi lived her life to the fullest, unafraid and full of joy. Those who met her and who knew her were indeed touched by an Angel. "

In the wake of Hiawayi’s death, Alabama lawmaker’s passed the “Hiawayi Robinson Alert Law,” which requires Alabama law enforcement agencies to publicize missing children.
cases.narrative:
On 9/18/2015, her body was found by a city public works employee, a little more than a mile from her home, in an area that is overgrown with grass and is used as a dumping ground for garbage, including appliances along Rebel Rd. Underneath and next to the body was trash.

Hiawayi's right arm was bent at the elbow. Her left arm was at a 45-degree angle, and her wrist was on top of a wooden cross that just happened to be in the debris, said Agent Deric Taylor of the State Bureau of Investigations. Hiawayi's Hello Kitty T-shirt was pulled up above her navel. Her right leg was extended outward, and her left leg was bent at the knee, Taylor said.

"The purple shorts as well as the underwear that she was wearing were pulled off the right leg and were just hanging on the left leg basically where the knee is," Taylor said.

The Mobile County District Attorney's Office believes Hiawayi died during a sexual assault.

An anal swab tested positive for seminal fluid, but the swab was contaminated, Taylor said. Taylor said DNA testing could not be performed on the swab.

A medical examination of her body showed that her cause of death was positional asphyxiation. She was also found to have been sexually assaulted and sodomized. The prosecution claimed she suffocated while her father sodomized her. Semen was found on her tshirt, but no DNA linked the crime to her father, as the sample was contaminated.
